evals.name: Vanilla JS contact form integration
evals.prompt: I have a plain HTML/CSS/JS website at https://myportfolio.dev and I want to add a contact form so visitors can reach me at hello@myportfolio.dev. The form should collect name, email, and message. I already have the email worker deployed at https://email-service.myaccount.workers.dev. Wire it up.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step integration including: adding myportfolio.dev to ALLOWED_ORIGINS in wrangler.toml, a complete HTML form, a JavaScript fetch POST to the /send endpoint with the correct payload shape, an HTML email template, client-side validation, and loading/success/error UX handling.

assertions.text: Response instructs the user to add myportfolio.dev to ALLOWED_ORIGINS in wrangler.toml
Response includes a command to redeploy the worker (e.g., npm run deploy)
Response includes a JavaScript fetch call using POST method targeting the /send endpoint
The fetch payload in the response includes 'to', 'from', 'subject', and 'html' fields
Response includes a replyTo field set to the visitor's email so the owner can reply directly
Response includes an HTML string for the email body rather than sending raw plain text user input
Response mentions showing a success or error message to the user after form submission

evals.name: React 'Request a Quote' form integration
evals.prompt: I'm building a React app for a plumbing company at https://quickplumb.co. I need a 'Request a Quote' form that collects customer name, phone, service type (dropdown: Leak Repair, Drain Cleaning, Installation), and preferred date. When submitted it should email quotes@quickplumb.co. The worker URL is https://email-service.plumbingco.workers.dev. Use React with useState for form state.
evals.expected_output: A complete React component with controlled form inputs, a POST to the worker's /send endpoint, CORS setup instructions for quickplumb.co, a branded HTML email template that includes all form fields, and proper loading/disabled-button/error state handling.

assertions.text: Response mentions adding quickplumb.co to ALLOWED_ORIGINS in wrangler.toml
Response includes React useState hook for managing form field values
Response includes a fetch or axios POST to https://email-service.plumbingco.workers.dev/send
The 'to' field in the POST payload is set to quotes@quickplumb.co
The HTML email template in the response includes the service type field from the form
Response includes logic to disable the submit button while the request is in flight

evals.name: Edge case: user requests email with file attachments
evals.prompt: I need to send emails from my website with PDF attachments — users submit a form and we email them a receipt PDF. Can I use your Cloudflare email worker for this?
evals.expected_output: A clear explanation that the current email worker does not support attachments, with a suggestion to use an alternative approach or service for attachment support.

assertions.text: Response explicitly states that the current worker does not support file attachments
Response suggests an alternative approach or service for sending emails with attachments (e.g., direct SendGrid API, a different service, or a future enhancement)
